transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-03-04
- Start time: 15:30 PT
- Duration: ~50 minutes
- Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Rajeev (Verdant Head of ML), Monica (Verdant Dir Infra), Ethan (Verdant Procurement)

[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone thanks for joining, hope the calendar time still works, we've got about 50 minutes on the agenda to run through renewal options, capacity, and the multi-region ask.
[00:18] Rajeev: Yep good, thanks Sofia. Quick context - our current contract ends mid-April and Q3 usage projections show about 2.5x token growth, mostly from inference qps for the recommendations service.
[00:30] Liam: Got it. When you say 2.5x is that steady state or peak?
[00:35] Rajeev: That's steady state, peaks could be 4x during batch updates. We wanted to talk about reserved GPU pools and burst capacity.
[00:45] Sofia: Sounds reasonable. We chatted earlier about Dedicated reserved pools — we can size a committed pool or do hybrid (dedicated + burst on host). Monica, you had questions about regions?
[00:58] Monica: Yes. We need eu-west-1 for residency and ap-southeast-1 for latency to APAC customers. Right now everything is in us-west. Can Redwood support replication of dedicated pools across those regions and what's the process?
[01:12] Liam: Short answer: yes. We support dedicated pools per region. The work is in provisioning and kernel selection for the model variants per region. There are a couple of tradeoffs: cross-region KV cache is not shared so cold-start for new region could be higher, and cost increases with duplicated capacity.
[01:30] Rajeev: How long does provisioning normally take? We can't have major downtime for a live service.
[01:36] Liam: For Dedicated, once PO is in and capacity is committed, typical provisioning is 3-5 business days per region in our hosted fleet; on-prem/private it's longer — depends on customer infra. We can do canary routing so traffic shifts gradually, no downtime.
[01:51] Ethan: From procurement side we need committed pricing tiers. Sofia, can you send pricing options for 12 vs 24 month terms and a committed v burst mix? Also any credits for multi-region commit?
[02:03] Sofia: Absolutely — I'll put together a sheet with 12/24 options, committed baseline, burst rates, and a tiered discount for multi-region commit. Expect it by Friday (2026-03-06).
[02:12] Rajeev: One more technical thing — model variants. We're using a quantized 8-bit model in prod now, but for certain low-latency flows we need a higher perf variant. Does Redwood support pinning different model variants to routes?
[02:26] Liam: Yes, per-route model pinning is supported. You can route a subset of traffic to a lower-latency variant and keep others on cheaper quantized when acceptable. There are also autoscale and fallback policies if a variant becomes unhealthy.
[02:40] Monica: On Private deployment — we need to understand audit logs and KMS integration. Our security team insists on HSM-backed keys for any PII-related inference.
[02:50] Liam: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and can integrate with HSMs via your key provider. Audit logs are available with per-request metadata; retention is configurable as an add-on. I'll share our security pack with redacted samples.
[03:05] Sofia: We'll attach the SOC2 / ISO docs to the follow-up email. Monica, can you list any additional compliance docs you need?
[03:12] Monica: Primarily SOC2 Type II, ISO27001, and evidence of network segmentation for VPCs. Also the process for on-prem upgrades.
[03:22] Liam: Noted. For network segmentation we provide a VPC deployment guide; for on-prem we have an ops runbook. Expect those links in follow-up.
[03:30] Rajeev: Back to capacity — do you have cost-per-token estimates for a dedicated pool vs hosted burst for our current model? Our finance team needs unit economics.
[03:43] Sofia: We do. I'll include a cost-per-1M-token estimate for committed capacity and for burst-on-host along with assumptions (seq length, batching). The spreadsheet will include latency buckets so you can compare.
[03:53] Ethan: Also want to confirm SLAs. If we commit to dedicated, what's the downtime SLA and credits?
[04:00] Sofia: Dedicated comes with an SLA (99.9% monthly uptime) and credits scale with severity. We'll include SLA wording in the contract options.
[04:08] Rajeev: On benchmarking — can Redwood run a quick latency bench using our prompt set in eu-west-1 so we can compare to us-west numbers?
[04:16] Liam: Yes — we can run a controlled microbenchmark. We'll need your prompt set and a small amount of sample traffic or a script. I can run it in eu-west-1 and ap-southeast-1 and share results within 3 business days.
[04:28] Rajeev: I'll put together the prompt set and traffic script.
[04:31] Sofia: Great. Any concerns about vendor lock or moving models between regions?
[04:36] Monica: IT is worried about lock-in, especially if we want to self-host later. What does the migration path look like?
[04:44] Liam: We support model export formats and can provide a private deployment package. For on-prem, migration requires providing compatible hardware and network setup; our ops team will assist with a migration plan. It's not instantaneous but feasible.
[04:56] Ethan: Procurement question — if we do a 24-month commit across 3 regions, do we get a better rate and does that lock us in?
[05:04] Sofia: We provide steeper discounts for longer-term, multi-region commits but we also include migration assistance and exit terms in the contract — we'll map those out so you have options.
[05:15] Rajeev: Anything we should be aware of re: model performance across regions? Like kernel selection differences?
[05:22] Liam: Kernel selection and GPU backend can vary by region/hardware; small latency differences expected. That's why we do per-region perf profiles and we can recommend quantization or different instance types.
[05:33] Sofia: Quick recap: action items — I'll send pricing + contract options by Friday, Liam will run region benchmarks and send infra docs, Rajeev and Monica to surface traffic, compliance list and timelines. We'll schedule a deeper technical session the week of March 16th.
[05:50] Monica: Sounds good. Can we get the pricing doc and security pack in one email for sharing with internal stakeholders?
[05:56] Sofia: Yes — single email with attachments and links.
[06:00] Ethan: Thanks everyone. One last ask — can you highlight any potential cost optimizations specifically for recommendations (long seqs, high qps)?
[06:08] Liam: Sure — we'll include batching recommendations, prefix caching, and quantization profiles. Also note rerouting some non-critical traffic to cheaper variants.
[06:18] Rajeev: Great, thanks.
[06:20] Sofia: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the sheet and schedule the deep-dive.

End of transcript. Some ASR imperfections: a few names transcribed as small variations, and timestamps approximate. Shared artifacts: pricing spreadsheet (link: https://redwood.example/pricing/vf-q1-2026), security pack (link: https://redwood.example/security-pack), region-bench template (link: https://redwood.example/bench-template).
